title: Pattern recognition: TLRs
objective: Explain how pattern-recognition receptors detect conserved microbial molecules, using TLR4 as the example.

steps.title: Sensing 'non-self' patterns
steps.body:
Innate cells can't know every pathogen, so they recognize **conserved molecular patterns** shared by whole classes of microbes, called [[PAMP|PAMPs]] (pathogen-associated molecular patterns).

The sensors are **[[pattern recognition receptor|pattern-recognition receptors (PRRs)]]**. The most famous family is the **[[Toll-like receptor|Toll-like receptors (TLRs)]]**.

steps.title: From flies to mammals
steps.body:
The Toll gene was first found controlling development and then antifungal defense in *Drosophila* (1996). Mammals turned out to have a whole family of Toll-*like* receptors.

A landmark result (1998): mouse strains that couldn't respond to bacterial **LPS** (a molecule in Gram-negative bacterial walls) carried mutations in **[[TLR4]]**. That pinned TLR4 as the LPS sensor.

steps.prompt: Match each sensor to what it detects.
steps.explanation: PRRs read molecular 'barcodes' of microbial classes, which is how a prebuilt system covers pathogens it has never seen.

steps.scenario: Two mouse strains are injected with LPS. You measure an inflammatory cytokine response.
options: TLR4 is required to sense LPS and trigger the response
Strain B has no immune cells
steps.explanation: Losing the response when the gene is mutated is loss-of-function evidence that TLR4 is the LPS sensor, the same necessity logic used throughout the sensory lessons.
steps.followUp: This is a direct parallel to knockout logic in A3/A4: break the candidate, lose the response.

steps.prompt: Why is TLR4 relevant to neuroscience?
options: TLRs are also expressed by glia and some neurons, so the nervous system can directly sense microbial and danger signals
steps.explanation: PRR signaling in glia and neurons is one route by which infection and tissue damage change neural activity, a recurring theme in neuroimmunology (B4–B7).

flag.note: Which neural cells express which TLRs, and to what effect, is an active and nuanced area.

sources.note: Toll controls the antifungal response in Drosophila.
LPS-unresponsive mouse strains carry Tlr4 mutations: TLR4 senses LPS.
